text:
maria: Heads up — noticed a handful of users still showing admin perms after last night's group-sync split. Not sure they should have them anymore.
omar: saw the same in audit-monitor. group external_id changed during the split and the deprovision job couldn't match; bindings left behind.
jenna: confirmed. roughly 12 accounts in tenant acme-inc with elevated roles. quick query I ran: 
```
SELECT user_email, role, binding_id, group_ext_id FROM role_bindings WHERE tenant='acme-inc' AND source='provisioner' AND revoked_at IS NULL;
```
evan: possible KMS exposure? if admins persisted we should consider rotating grants or at least marking keys as under review. any evidence they used keys? short window but we need to be cautious.
security-bot: automated alert created: SEC-472 — unusual role reassignments (12 users). Assigning severity pending human triage.
sanford: quick theory: batch splitter in the provisioner creates ephemeral group external_ids when we split big groups into subgroups. parallel deprov job looked up by previous external_id and failed to remove internal bindings that referenced internal group ids. TL;DR: split -> new ext_id -> some bindings orphaned.
maria: ok mitigation plan: run the reconcile tool in dry-run to verify what would be removed, then apply. I don't want to run blind because of rate limits and customer impact. snippet:
```
./bin/provisioner reconcile --tenant acme-inc --since="2026-03-19T22:00:00Z" --dry-run
```
omar: i ran the dry-run earlier: it reports 12 orphaned role_bindings that would be deleted, and 3 KMS grant principals that look like grp-temp-xxxx. sample dry-run output: 
```
DRY RUN: remove binding 98765 (user: alice@acme) -> group: grp-temp-9f3a
DRY RUN: remove kms_grant id=gr-4321 principal=grp-temp-9f3a
```
jenna: recommended order: 1) dry-run, 2) back up role_bindings table, 3) apply reconcile, 4) revoke KMS grants, 5) rotate keys if suspicious. Who's oncall to run apply?
sre-oncall: I'm oncall and can run apply at 10:15 PT. prefer doing it in a maintenance window and throttled to avoid token storms.
evan: important: hold on revoking KMS grants until we have forensic events — audit-ingest had a lag last night and some events might not have been indexed. If we revoke too early we lose evidence. Where are raw KMS logs? cloud-kms -> key-usage logs -> storage bucket raw-events.
maria: good catch. I see audit-ingest had an error between 01:10-03:15 UTC (ingest-batch-6 crashed). that explains missing deprov events. we need to backfill from the raw bucket before revokes.
omar: I'll kick off audit backfill now: 
```
./tools/audit-backfill --from 2026-03-19T01:00:00Z --to 2026-03-19T03:30:00Z --tenant acme-inc
```
jenna: creating incident playbook steps in the PM (short checklist): backfill -> reconcile dry-run -> apply reconcile -> check post-reconcile access scan -> revoke KMS grants -> rotate if usage observed -> customer notification.
sre-oncall: running reconcile apply now (throttle=5/s). will post results.
deploy-bot: deploy notice: provisioner v2.17.4 deployed to canary (5%) commit abc123 — includes small fix to group id mapping edge-case. :rocket:
maria: after reconcile we should run the access-eval to ensure no residual inherited permissions remain. also schedule a short read-only window to revoke KMS grants safely.
omar: note for postmortem: add root cause "non-deterministic temp group ext_id generation during batch split" and mitigations: deterministic id allocator + stronger reconciliation criteria + fallback matching by member list.
jenna: assigning owners and timeline: maria (incident lead/security), omar (provisioner owner), evan (kms forensics), sanford (audit backfill owner). target: initial remediation done by EOD tomorrow.
sre-oncall: reconcile finished — 12 bindings removed, 0 errors. logs here: s3://prod-logs/provisioner/reconcile/1768459-apply.log
maria: thanks — next step: run KMS grant revoke after backfill completes. omar/evan coordinate.
evan: backfill finished, found the missing deprov events; no suspicious key usage in that window. proceeding with revoke of the 3 stale grants now. command: 
```
cloud-kms revoke-grant --key projects/rw/keys/teams-acme --grant-id gr-4321
```
jenna: once revokes are done we'll update SEC-472 and prepare a short customer notification template (sensitive to avoid over-alarming).
security-bot: SEC-472 updated: remediation applied, incident severity S2, postmortem pending.

maria: we'll follow up with a postmortem that includes a timeline, root cause, and the longer-term engineering fixes: deterministic group IDs, strengthening deprov lookup (fall back to member-set diff), and end-to-end test for split+reconcile.
omar: opening PR for allocator change and adding deterministic tag to ext_id: https://git.internal/rw/provisioner/pulls/452 (WIP)
sre-oncall: all done from my side. if anyone notices lingering access, ping me and i'll run targeted revocations.
maria: great work everyone. postmortem owner = jenna. i'll draft customer comms and legal/security review. :thumbsup:
